# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Give desktop work desktop control

Read [Designing for macOS](../../references/designing-for-macos.md). Inspect the current task, document/content model, windows, commands, and interruption behavior. Determine whether the request is a design, review, or port. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish observed behavior from proposals or missing runtime evidence.

Choose window boundaries around useful units of work. If documents or parallel comparisons benefit from independent windows, retain their own selections and edits. If one workspace suffices, make it resizable and avoid unnecessary modal navigation. Plan full screen for focused work without making it the only usable arrangement. Keep essential commands reachable even when a window is partly offscreen.

Build a command inventory from the task. Put app commands in the menu bar, give common operations appropriate shortcuts, and ensure a keyboard-only completion path. Align toolbar/contextual controls with those same actions and availability states. Use pointer precision for selection and editing rather than inflating a phone-style interface across the display. Read [the text-view guide](../../references/text-views.md). This operating procedure is application advice; use the guide for platform qualifications.

Inspect the supplied content, view/code, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Determine whether the text is long or formatted, editable or read-only, and useful to copy elsewhere. Choose a text view for lengthy, specially formatted, or multiline editable content; use a label for short static text and a field for short entry. Preserve leading alignment and system color behavior where appropriate. Decide how long content reflows rather than truncating information the task requires. Match the iOS/iPadOS keyboard to expected input. On tvOS use text views for display and fields for editing, minimizing entry; do not copy a phone's long-form editor unchanged. Decision: people need to read the full report and copy its reference numbers without editing them. After: a read-only multiline text view reflows and scrolls, permits selection/copy, and preserves contextual formatting; identifiers remain actual text.

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Mirror meaning rather than every pixel

Read [Right to left](../../references/right-to-left.md). Inspect target language/region, text samples, custom layout/assets, and the intended task. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Preserve the existing framework's directional behavior before adding manual overrides; mark locale-specific assumptions requiring native-language review.

Classify each directional element. Reading-order navigation, progress controls, endpoint labels, and meaningful ordered image collections generally reverse position/direction. Literal physical directions or controls aimed at a specific onscreen place retain that meaning. Preserve photographs, logos, universal signs, and ordinary object/tool handedness; localize strongly directional art rather than blindly flipping it.

Handle text at the right level. Short labels follow interface alignment; longer paragraphs follow their own language, including mixed-language content. Keep list alignment consistent even when one entry uses another script. Preserve digit order in numbers, phones, and card numbers while adapting locale-specific numeral/currency formatting and the position of ordered sequences.

Use directional/localized SF Symbol variants. Review a custom complex glyph component by component: its base, badge position, actual text, and negation slash can have different needs. If Latin uppercase neighbors Arabic/Hebrew labels, evaluate optical balance rather than assuming equal numeric point size looks equal. Hardware-linked controls retain any platform-specific physical placement instead of inheriting a generic mirror rule.

**Worked transformation:** Before, an Arabic cycling app flips the map photo, bicycle glyph, phone digits, and Back arrow together. Decision: only reading-order navigation should mirror; the other elements describe real content or fixed sequences. After, Back and progress order adapt, the map/photo and bicycle handedness remain correct, and phone digits retain their internal order under localized formatting.

Deliver a corrected directional screen/asset mapping or implementation. Fail if reading-order navigation points the wrong way, digits reverse internally, real artwork changes meaning, or a mixed-language paragraph follows the wrong alignment. Use representative content in actual layout; screenshots cannot verify keyboard/cursor/bidirectional editing behavior.

# Make commands discoverable and preserve familiar keys

Read [Keyboards](../../references/keyboards.md). Inspect task commands, text-entry contexts, current bindings, supported platforms/locales, and requested design/review/adaptation. Physical keyboards are covered on every listed platform except watchOS. Preserve the existing stack and identify actual keyboard evidence before claiming complete navigation.

Build a command inventory from frequent actions. Reuse familiar standard shortcuts for their expected meanings; consult the guide's mapping in context rather than treating legacy/system entries as universally available app APIs. A standard combination may serve another meaning only when its normal action has no place in this app. Avoid deriving an unrelated command by adding modifiers to a familiar one.

For app-specific commands, prefer a learnable Command-based combination, Shift for related variants, and sparing Option; avoid Control conflicts. Check international keyboards where Option makes characters. Preserve expected modifier-drag/resize behavior and clear smallest-increment arrow adjustment. Games may use single keys and customization while retaining system actions.

Trace ordinary content focus and Full Keyboard Access separately. On iPad, content/text/sidebar/collection focus is not proof that every button/switch is reachable; Full Keyboard Access supplies the broader route. Preserve accessibility shortcuts. On visionOS, make each Command-discoverability title meaningful without submenu context because the displayed list is flattened.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a diagram app uses Command-C to create a shape, binds Control-based shortcuts for everything, and has an unreachable Done button. Decision: copy semantics and a complete keyboard task outweigh shortcut novelty. After, Command-C copies selection, shape creation gets a suitable distinct command, and focus/activation can reach Done; the command title explains itself in discoverability UI.

Deliver a corrected command/binding inventory and keyboard task path or implementation. Fail if text editing invokes an unrelated command, shortcuts collide with system access, or the task cannot finish without a pointer. Actual OS shortcuts, international layouts, and Full Keyboard Access need supported-device execution; static binding inspection is narrower evidence.

# Keep hidden content reachable and location stable

Read [the scroll-view guide](../../references/scroll-views.md). The workflow is application advice; distinguish platform input capabilities from behavior actually enabled in the app.

Inspect overflow content, scroll axes/owners, selected or inserted content, floating controls, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Record nested containers, indicators, zoom limits, and automatic reveal logic from evidence. A screenshot cannot prove gesture conflicts or Look to Scroll support.

Preserve system gestures/keys/elastic feedback and avoid same-axis nested scrolling; orthogonal nesting can be appropriate. Suggest offscreen content beyond transient indicators. Reveal search results, insertion points, and relevant selections only as far as necessary, preserving context. For paged content retain overlap/context and avoid a redundant same-axis scroll indicator when page controls serve that role. Bound zoom to useful scales.

Implement the scroll/reveal model or provide axis/ownership/position/edge-effect specification; reviews identify concrete unreachable or jumping content. Apply scroll-edge effects only where floating controls overlap content, generally automatic and one per view, with aligned split-pane heights. On TV scrolling follows focus. On watch favor vertical Crown content. On visionOS leave indicator space; Look to Scroll is per-view opt-in for suitable reading/browsing, requires clear boundaries and removal of custom parallax/scroll effects, and is unsuitable for precise secondary controls.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a long note scrolls inside a same-axis page scroller, and typing recenters the whole document on every character. Decision: competing owners and excessive reveal destroy location. After: use one primary vertical owner and scroll only enough to expose the insertion point, retaining surrounding lines.

Prefer automatic styling; it provides stronger separation for dense toolbars, uncontained text, or pinned headers. Thoroughly test legibility if choosing soft styling. The hard style gives a more defined opaque boundary; the soft style fades through a variable blur. Use an effect only where floating controls overlap a scroll view, not as decoration or a dark overlay. Suppress the scroll indicator on that same axis to avoid redundant signals. ### macOS Scroll indicators are also called scroll bars. Apply it consistently across comparable content. Full-width or full-height regions give generous, understandable boundaries; inset regions need clear edges. Remove custom scroll-position effects such as parallax or animation before enabling it to prevent unpredictable behavior. ### watchOS Prefer vertical content that works with the Digital Crown. Use vertical tab views for page-based navigation, with an indicator beside the crown. Keep pages near one screen tall when possible; long pages can scroll and the page indicator expands into a scroll indicator. Use variable heights sparingly and preferably after short fixed pages. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Page controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/page-controls) [Gestures](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures) [Pointing devices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pointing-devices) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit — WatchKit — SwiftUI ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026, March 24, 2026, July 28, 2025, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 5, 2023.

Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Leave enough focus padding for system enlargement so focused items do not obscure important information. #### Grids Use consistent row/column spacing, sufficient room for enlargement, and symmetrical partial items at both horizontal edges. Add extra separation above and below row titles. UIKit collection flow layout derives the column count from item width and spacing. Source grid measurements follow; all use 40 pt horizontal gaps and a minimum 100 pt vertical gap between unfocused rows. #### Two-column grid Unfocused item width: 860 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Three-column grid Unfocused item width: 560 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Four-column grid Unfocused item width: 410 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Five-column grid Unfocused item width: 320 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Eight-column grid Unfocused item width: 184 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Nine-column grid Unfocused item width: 160 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. ### visionOS Support resizing in windows and volumes; center content horizontally at very large sizes. Set minimum/maximum bounds only to avoid overlaps or unwieldy layouts, not to disable resizing. Use inline 3D content sparingly for meaningful additions; inset it so it avoids controls and window edges. Prefer volumes or immersive spaces for large/model-centric content. Open supplemental content in an adjacent window, reserving ornaments for interactive app controls. Space controls so hover feedback remains distinct; regular buttons should have centers at least 60 pt apart. ### watchOS Normally use no more than three glyph buttons or two text buttons side by side. Full-width text controls usually work best; two short labels can fit on a non-scrolling screen. Support autorotation when people may show content, such as a photo or QR code, to another person or reader instead of always sleeping on wrist-away movement. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026, September 9, 2025, June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, September 9, 2024, June 10, 2024, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, September 15, 2023, June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.

# Keep the interaction target distinct from the chosen value

Read [Focus and selection](../../references/focus-and-selection.md). Inspect platform/input, focus groups, selected state, dynamic content, and supplied implementation. Establish design/review/adaptation mode. The guide's component-focus model excludes iOS/watchOS; visionOS gaze hover is a different system.

Map focus movement separately from activation and persistent selection. Focus may select automatically only when that does not unexpectedly shift context; tvOS normally needs separate activation. Use system effects and avoid moving focus without input. If an item disappears during discrete directional movement, choose a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide the indicator rather than inventing the next destination.

On iPad, group custom content so Tab moves among logical groups and arrows move within them in expected reading order; prioritize the likely entry item. Ordinary content focus coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls. On TV, every interactive item needs directional reachability and room for enlarged focus art. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, selected, and unavailable states distinct. Full-screen gestures should manipulate visible content rather than invisible focus.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a TV watchlist opens each item as focus passes over it and uses the same glow for focus and Saved. Decision: navigation must not activate content, and persistent choice must survive focus movement. After, focus raises/highlights the item, Select opens it, and a filled saved indicator remains as focus moves; unavailable items are inactive and unreachable.

Deliver a focus-route/group map and state contract or implementation. Walk each entry, direction, activation, return, and removal scenario. Fail if a control cannot be reached/exited, focus jumps without input, selected state vanishes with focus, or enlargement obscures information. Source inspection can establish intended grouping; actual focus engines, remote behavior, and Full Keyboard Access need supported execution.

Use [Remotes](../apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md) for TV button meanings, [Keyboards](../apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for shortcuts/access, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) when the request actually concerns gaze feedback.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Revised Mac long-form note interaction specification

## Scope and evidence

"'`interface.md` reports that notes are screenshots, editing cannot select text, formatting resets scrolling, read-only notes show an active insertion cursor, and content includes long URLs and mixed scripts. These are supplied descriptions, not independently reproduced defects. This specification replaces that behavior; it does not implement an editor or assume an Apple SDK.

The primary task is sustained reading, selecting and copying, with editing when permission allows. Use a resizable Mac document workspace, a persistent textual note body, and one vertical scrolling owner. Keep app commands reachable through the menu bar in a Mac host; an implementation must supply an equivalent discoverable command surface if its host cannot integrate there. Preserve selection and work across app activation changes. These decisions follow [Designing for macOS, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos#Best-practices).

## Decisions

### Actual text and independent permissions

Represent the note as Unicode text plus formatting spans and stable paragraph identifiers. Render a multiline, selectable text surface in both states. Screenshots may be supplementary previews, but cannot be the reading/editing representation. Retrieve original text and formatting for existing screenshot notes; if unavailable, mark migration unresolved rather than silently treating OCR as authoritative.

This follows the recommendation to choose a text view for lengthy or formatted content and allow useful text to be selected and copied: [Text views, Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views#Best-practices). “Text view” here describes capabilities, not a particular class or framework.

| Capability | Read-only | Editable |
|---|---|---|
| Read, scroll, select across lines, Select All, Copy, Find | Available | Available |
| Text insertion caret | Never shown | Shown only when body has input focus and an insertion target |
| Selection highlight and keyboard focus indication | Available; distinct from an insertion caret | Available |
| Type, paste, cut, delete, drop text, format, undo/redo mutations | Rejected at the command/model boundary | Available for valid target and permission |
| Status | Persistent “Read-only” with known reason, if supplied | “Editable” and save status |

Read-only does not disable the entire body: it remains focusable and selectable. Typing must neither mutate text nor silently change mode. Do not invent a reason for missing permission. A pointer text-selection cursor can remain appropriate in either mode; the misleading behavior being removed is the active insertion caret.

Open according to authoritative write permission; do not require an extra Edit mode for writable notes. Permission changes update the same surface without rebuilding the document. On revocation, stop mutations immediately, finish or cancel composition without committing unauthorized text, retain existing unsaved work as a recoverable draft, and display “Read-only — unsaved changes retained” when applicable. Restoring permission retains selection and viewport; do not unexpectedly focus the body or show a caret until it has input focus. These transition details are product decisions.

### Reading, reflow and scripts

Use semantic title, body and supporting-status roles. Prefer the host'"'s system text font with appropriate script fallback; otherwise use a legible installed font stack. Initial product choices: body 15 pt Regular, line height approximately 1.4 times body size, title 22 pt Semibold, supporting text 13 pt. These are proposed defaults, not HIG-mandated editor dimensions. Prefer a reading column around 70 body-character widths, shrinking to available width with margins; use all necessary vertical space.

Provide View > Text Size at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175% and 200%, plus reset. This scales presentation and controls without changing saved formatting. Reflow and expand controls; no essential text is truncated. Support an optional heavier reading weight without changing document styles. macOS has no Dynamic Type; this is an explicit accommodation. Loose leading and adaptable hierarchy are supported by [Typography](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#Using-system-fonts), its [macOS qualification](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#macOS), and [Accessibility, Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

Wrap paragraphs to the column. Permit an unbroken URL to wrap visually at safe character/grapheme boundaries when needed; never insert spaces, hyphens or newlines into stored/copied content. Do not ellipsize, clip, or require horizontal scrolling to read prose or URLs. Copy returns the selected underlying text; a full selected URL remains byte-for-byte equivalent in its original encoding after round-trip serialization.

Use a Unicode-aware shaping and bidirectional text engine. Paragraph alignment follows its own language/direction; short interface labels follow interface direction.
